## Must-Fix 1 — the predicate conflates "history REWRITTEN" with "remote genuinely DIVERGED", and the guard prose then forbids the correct recovery for the second state

**Defect.** `origin/issue-<N>` exists AND is not an ancestor of `HEAD` is true in **two** states,
not one:

- **(a)** the rewritten branch — the #2296 target this task exists for;
- **(b)** a genuinely diverged branch — the remote carries novel FOREIGN commits while local
  carries unpushed commits. This is not hypothetical: pod-side result pushes are a named fleet
  channel (`.claude/rules/pod-side-reporting.md`, "pushing result commits"), and state (b) is
  precisely what the existing pull-retry pair exists to self-heal (SKILL.md L13080-13082:
  "Push retry mirrors CLAUDE.md § Concurrent repo-root committers: pull --rebase=merges
  --autostash then re-push on a rejected push").

Under plan v1, Hunk A's comment asserts a false biconditional — non-ancestry ⇒ "the branch history
was REWRITTEN" (§4 L71-73) — and the Hunk B echo orders "do NOT push, do NOT pull, do NOT
force-push … run the § Rewritten-branch landing route" (§4 L115). For state (b) that forbids the
sanctioned recovery, and the route it points at is unreachable: landing-route precondition 1
requires a PASSing lint verdict, which does not exist mid-run. A Step-5 round push that copies
canonical snippet (1) into state (b) is therefore left with **no sanctioned action**. The
acceptance-4 discharge (§2 row 4) silently narrows "ordinary" to fast-forward + missing-ref, and
§7's fixture table has no (b) arm.

**Why this is Must-Fix even though nothing lands wrong.** The critic verified the ROUTING is
fail-safe: landing-route precondition 2 (§4 L281-290) already enumerates remote-only content and
cherry-picks-or-surfaces novel commits, and §17 correctly records why `git cherry` cannot serve as
the routing predicate (conflict-reconciled rebases read `+`). So no wrong content reaches `main`.
But the deliverable of this task IS recipe prose the fleet treats as binding, and v1 ships (i) a
false diagnosis inside the most-copied snippet in the file, (ii) wrong recovery advice for a real
recurring state, and (iii) a mid-run dead end. Frequency is moderated by tracking-ref staleness — a
pod push does not update the VM's `refs/remotes/origin/issue-<N>`, so state (b) usually still
reaches the old pull-retry via the guard-false → push-rejected race — but Hunk C's own branch fetch
refreshes that ref, making the zero-PR arm block **reliably** in state (b).

**Fix — mechanism unchanged; wording, enumeration, and one fixture arm.**

1. Add the diverged-remote row to the §7 truth table and to the Hunk A/B comment text:
   non-ancestry means "rewritten **OR** remote-diverged". Keep fail-closed routing for both — no
   mechanical discriminator exists, which is §17's own argument.
2. Reword the guard echoes: replace the flat "do NOT pull" with the DISCRIMINATION STEP —
   inspect the remote-only commits (`log --oneline HEAD..origin/issue-<N>` plus
   `cherry HEAD origin/issue-<N>`); all-novel FOREIGN work (e.g. pod result commits) ⇒ the
   ordinary pull-rebase recovery is correct; anything that is or may be this branch's superseded
   own payload ⇒ the landing route; mixed ⇒ landing route plus cherry-pick. This is the same
   judgment precondition 2 already encodes, surfaced AT the guard instead of only inside the route.
3. Give the canonical-snippet (Hunk A) copy-site reader its MID-RUN instruction: the landing route
   is a Step-10d procedure; mid-run the branch stays unpushed and the session surfaces — never
   attempt the route without a verdict.
4. Preferably add one fixture arm — shared-history remote plus one foreign remote commit plus local
   commits — pinning whichever routing text lands.

[long-phase-heartbeat] Measured probe CORRECTS a plan v2 claim — strictly-behind push is REJECTED, not exit-0

Plan v2 (critic-revise draft, not yet persisted) claimed that in the strictly-ahead-remote state
the ordinary push is "a no-op exit-0 `Everything up-to-date` (today's behavior)". That is wrong.
Measured directly rather than reasoned about, because the claim is load-bearing twice: it is the
byte-compatibility argument for the reverse-leg narrowing (§7 / §12 A14) AND an assertion in
fixture test 8 arm 3, which would have failed the moment it landed.

## The probe

Synthetic repo (no repo state touched, torn down after): bare origin; work clone; base commit on
`main`; branch `issue-99` + payload P1 pushed with `-u`; a second "pod" clone adds foreign commit
F1 and pushes it to `issue-99` (the documented #1205 result-push channel); back in the work clone,
`fetch origin` with NO local novelty ⇒ local strictly behind.

```
leg1  merge-base --is-ancestor origin/issue-99 HEAD   rc=1
leg2  merge-base --is-ancestor HEAD origin/issue-99   rc=0
git push origin issue-99                              rc=1
 ! [rejected]        issue-99 -> issue-99 (non-fast-forward)
hint: Updates were rejected because the tip of your current branch is behind
hint: its remote counterpart.
```

## What survives, what changes

**The predicate is CORRECT** — leg2 rc=0 means the guard does not fire and a strictly-ahead remote
routes to the ordinary push arm, exactly as the reverse-leg narrowing intends. The two-leg
mutual-non-ancestry design is unaffected.

**The mechanism claim was wrong.** Git reports "Everything up-to-date" only when the local ref is
the remote's tip or a descendant; a strictly-BEHIND local ref is a non-fast-forward update request
and is refused. The push is rejected and falls into the existing

## The sharper point this measurement produced

The refspec-less `pull --rebase=merges --autostash` is **correct** for a diverged-or-behind remote
(the branch's configured upstream IS the right rebase target) and **catastrophic** only when local
history was REWRITTEN — because only then does that same upstream hold SUPERSEDED copies of the
branch's own payload, so the rebase replays `main` as new objects (#1128 / #2296). The pull is not
unsafe in general. That is exactly why the fix must DISCRIMINATE rather than remove the pull, and
why all five pull sites stay intact inside the new `else` arms.

## Why the residual bucket stays a judgment step

Mutual non-ancestry is genuinely TWO states — (a) history rewritten, (b) the remote legitimately

five pull sites intact inside the new `else` arms — the refspec-less pull is CORRECT for a
behind-or-diverged remote and catastrophic only under rewritten history.
